Each investor is allotted units corresponding proportionally to their contribution, with daily portfolio value reflected through the Net Asset Value (NAV).

A fund with an NAV of ₹10 is not 'cheaper' or better positioned than a fund with an NAV of ₹500; both will generate identical rupee returns if their underlying securities appreciate by the same percentage. NAV simply reflects historical unit value growth and cumulative past compounding, not valuation attractiveness.

keyword: How does a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) work?

When markets decline, your fixed installment purchases more units at a lower NAV, and when markets advance, fewer units are acquired at a higher NAV—a mathematical principle known as rupee-cost averaging. This removes the behavioral hazard of timing market peaks and troughs while fostering long-term wealth compounding.

SEBI mandates statutory tiered caps on TER based on scheme asset size to ensure economies of scale benefit retail unit-holders.

Redemptions follow the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) accounting rule, so your oldest units exit first.
